mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر): the hāʾ refers back to the Qur'an, although there has been no mention of it, since the meaning is understood.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (وما أدراك ما ليلة القدر): the first (ما) is an interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (أدراك) is a verb containing the agent pronoun referring back to (ما), and the kāf is the first object of (أدراك). The second (ما) is an interrogative, a second mubtadaʾ, and (ليلة) is the khabar (predicate) of the second; the clause is in the position of the second object of (أدراك). (أدراك) with its two objects is the khabar of the first (ما). Its like is (وما أدراك ما القارعة). The discussion of this has already preceded in al-Ḥāqqa and elsewhere.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying (سلام هي): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
His saying (حتى مطلع الفجر): the base in the analogy of (مطلع) is fatḥa on the lām, because the noun of place and the maṣdar (verbal noun) of faʿala yafʿulu are on the pattern mafʿal. Some words are irregular and came with kasra as a dialect, such as (المسجد) and (المجلس). Al-Kisāʾī read (مطلع) with kasra on the lām, making it among those that depart from their analogy.
